speaker_role: admissions committee members (documentary footage; institution not named in transcript)
key_insights: Committee splits an applicant pool of roughly 8,000 into 30+ geographic regions, with two readers paired per region before full-committee discussion.
Even applicants with top test scores, all-A grades, varsity sports, and music honors are frequently sent to the waitlist because the pool is overwhelmingly strong.
Committee members explicitly describe the process as 'agonizing' and admit it comes down to 'minute distinctions' among similarly excellent candidates.
About 1,000 of the strongest files are escalated to be heard and voted on by the full committee rather than decided by the two initial readers alone.
Serious personal/family hardship (e.g., major financial loss, family instability) is raised as context that can function as a plus factor for an otherwise high-achieving student.
Legacy-type family ties (siblings already enrolled at the same university) are mentioned as a background fact in a file but are not shown deciding the outcome by themselves.
Committee members acknowledge sometimes voting on gut feeling rather than being able to fully articulate their reasoning for admit/waitlist calls.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Applicant pool of about 8,000 divided into 30+ geographic regions with two readers per region (stated by a committee member)
Roughly 1,000 candidates escalated to be heard by the full committee (stated by a committee member)

notable_or_distinctive: Rare real (or closely dramatized) audio of an actual admissions committee deliberating file-by-file, including morally complex personal circumstances, rather than a generic after-the-fact explainer.
